body.x: Linsol (CEO HYOKEUN LEE) participated in the Global Media Online Meet-Up on July 2, hosted in collaboration with U.S. tech media outlet Ubergizmo, targeting Korean companies and startups.

The Global Media Meet-Up, jointly hosted by AVING News and Ubergizmo, aims to introduce Korean companies’ products and technologies to the global market. It also offers a platform to pre-promote CES 2026 Innovation Award applicants and expand their business opportunities through global media exposure.

Headquartered in Daejeon, Linsol started as the first in-house venture of Hanwha Aerospace and became an independent company in 2023. Under the slogan “Hearing the Invisible, Protecting the Invaluable,” it develops cutting-edge acoustic intelligence solutions for critical infrastructure. Leveraging military-grade precision sound detection technology, it is rapidly expanding from defense to civilian sectors such as industrial safety, rescue, and mobility.

Its flagship products include the ‘Acoustic Eye’, a precision sound detection device, and the ‘Acoustic Tag’, a transmitter that emits ultrasonic signals to track real-time location. The Acoustic Eye detects invisible threats in environments like roads and homes, making it ideal for both industrial and general vehicles, as well as for detecting illegal drones in public security systems.

Linsol signed a large-scale demand contract worth 30 billion KRW over five years with Hyundai HD for a forklift-specific version of Acoustic Eye, solidifying its place in the industrial vehicle safety market. It also successfully delivered 2,000 units of Acoustic Tag to BLACKYAK I&C and is proceeding with further production.

body.cap: Acoustic Eye | Image provided by Linsol

body.x: Although Linsol has proven its technology in Korea through successful B2B partnerships, its global recognition remains low. To change that, the company plans to demonstrate its acoustic intelligence technology live at CES 2026 in Las Vegas, showcasing how its safety technology detects invisible threats through sound.

CES, the world’s largest tech trade show, attracts major ADAS and automotive brands like Tesla, Waymo, Bosch, and Denso, along with a wide range of consumer attention. Linsol aims to position itself globally as “Korea’s acoustic AI innovation leader,” paving the way for future expansion into smart home security solutions.

As concerns over privacy violations from illegal drones grow, Linsol offers a comprehensive security solution that protects not just homes but entire communities. Acoustic Eye detects threats within a 500-meter radius, covering blind spots left by traditional radar and camera systems, making it highly effective in environments such as homes, schools, hospitals, and corporate campuses.
Real-time alerts and monitoring are provided via a mobile app synced with indoor displays. It also enables integration with smart IoT ecosystems and safe drone neutralization features.

body.cap: Usage example of Acoustic Eye | Image provided by Linsol

body.x: Technologically, Acoustic Eye uses a multi-channel sensor module to detect everything from mini drones to large aircraft in noisy environments up to 500 meters away. Its AI algorithm distinguishes aerial threats from background noise and differentiates between authorized and unauthorized drones in real time. It can amplify aerial acoustic signals up to eight times, even detecting stealth drones.

A Linsol representative stated, “Acoustic Eye immediately detects aerial threats, alerts relevant agencies, and activates response measures to eliminate the response gap within the critical 3-minute golden time. While existing home security focuses on ground-level threats, Acoustic Eye monitors the full 3D airspace to eliminate blind spots and block threats that CCTVs can’t see.”

In addition to cutting-edge security tech, Acoustic Eye features a sleek, intuitive design that blends with residential environments. The device uses a magnetic mounting system for tool-free installation on windows, requiring no permanent modifications.

It offers a user-friendly app interface with real-time alerts, threat visualization, and automated responses. The product can integrate with smart home systems for instant actions, such as closing blinds or switching lights. Additionally, it includes a display for date, time, and temperature, combining aesthetic appeal with functionality.

body.cap: HYOKEUN LEE (second from left), CEO of Linsol, and Hubert Nguyen (second from right), CTO of Ubergizmo, pose for a commemorative photo with Linsol staff at the Global Media Meet-Up held at MIK Base Camp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on Wednesday, July 2 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Linsol highlights three innovation points for Acoustic Eye: militarized tech for civilians, securing the golden response time, and comprehensive aerial protection. These innovations enable real-time threat detection, immediate alerts, and rapid response.

The company has commercialized military-grade sonar detection from Korea’s Defense Technology Institute to identify even the stealthiest drones. Its patented technologies include a method for locating sound sources and a frequency analysis system using neural networks, offering military-level precision for consumers.

Unlike traditional systems that separate detection and response, Acoustic Eye integrates both, enabling immediate action before a privacy breach occurs. It protects previously vulnerable airspace using sound-only positioning technology, ensuring full 3D coverage.

As urban air mobility (UAM) transforms our skies, Acoustic Eye fulfills CES’s vision of “human security for all” by democratizing military-grade acoustic security. It reduces disaster-related economic losses and protects vulnerable populations from privacy and security threats.

body.cap: HYOKEUN LEE of Linsol responds to Q&A during the Global Media Meet-Up held at MIK Base Camp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on Wednesday, July 2 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Acoustic Eye redefines security by enabling not just personal homes but entire communities to move from reactive surveillance to proactive defense. By integrating detection and response within the golden time, it prevents privacy invasions, safety threats, and economic damages.
This paradigm shift creates an intelligent aerial threat detection and neutralization environment for apartments, schools, hospitals, and public facilities.
Leveraging domestic success, Linsol is targeting global markets. Its key partner prospects include Textron Systems (USA), Thales Group (France), and Axis Communications (Sweden).

Beyond CES 2026, Linsol plans to attend global expos such as MWC 2026 in Barcelona to unveil 5G/6G-connected mobility solutions and promote communication-based safety systems to attract telco and IoT platform partners.

At GITEX 2026 in Dubai, the company will showcase smart city security solutions, targeting Middle Eastern and African markets. It plans to supply Acoustic Eye to regional smart city projects and meet the safety needs of the oil and gas industries.

Linsol will also exhibit at industrial expos like Hannover Messe in Germany, introducing its acoustic safety solutions to Europe’s manufacturing sector. By partnering with vision sensor-based ADAS brands, it aims to position Acoustic Eye as a core solution to meet Euro NCAP 2025 blind spot detection mandates.
